superseded_reason: OPS-SERVED-SURFACE-CANARY-AND-CLAIM-TRUTH-W1 CH3. Superseded by audits/api-performance-public-shape-snapshot-2026-09-10.json, which carries the same allowed_keys and forbidden_keys plus the forbidden_VALUES contract this file lacked entirely. EXACTLY TWO KEYS WERE APPENDED HERE (superseded_by + superseded_reason) and nothing else was altered — no reserialization, no whitespace change, no value change; the per-file proof diff <(jq -S 'del(.superseded_by,.superseded_reason)' old) <(jq -S 'del(...)' new) is EMPTY and runs in the CH3 gate. The append is REQUIRED, not bookkeeping: scripts/build-knowledge-json.mjs projects EVERY audits/*-shape-snapshot-*.json into the PUBLIC knowledge bundle and src/lib/knowledge-index.ts keys each document response_shape:/api/performance-public, so two LIVE files carrying this endpoint are a duplicate document id, which winkBM25S rejects outright: KnowledgeIndex.build() THROWS (Error: winkBM25S: Duplicate document encountered: response_shape:<endpoint>), tests/integration/knowledge-flow.test.ts fails, and at runtime the lazily-constructed index behind search_knowledge / chat_knowledge cannot be built. MEASURED CORRECTION, kept visible because the instrument matters: `npm run build:knowledge` TOLERATES the duplicate and exits 0 reporting response_shapes=39, so the builder succeeding is NOT evidence the bundle is usable — the rejection lives in the INDEX, not the build. A non-empty superseded_by is the ONLY thing that excludes a snapshot from that projection. This file stays on disk: a dated ledger states what was true when written.
